cls: HCV NS5B nucleotide polymerase inhibitor (direct-acting antiviral)
quick: 400 mg PO once daily with a ribavirin-based regimen
Combination with ribavirin/peginterferon contraindicated in pregnancy
Presence in human milk unknown; weigh risk/benefit
No adjustment if mild/moderate; no recommendation if severe/ESRD
No adjustment Child-Pugh A/B/C; not studied in decompensated cirrhosis
HBV status before treatment; heart rate if on amiodarone; HCV RNA
summary: Sofosbuvir (Sovaldi) is a hepatitis C virus NS5B nucleotide polymerase inhibitor used as a component of combination antiviral therapy for chronic HCV genotypes 1-4 in adults and genotypes 2-3 in children >=3 years. The recommended dose is one 400 mg tablet once daily combined with ribavirin, with or without peginterferon alfa; genotype determines the partner regimen and duration. It carries a boxed warning for HBV reactivation and a warning for serious bradycardia when given with amiodarone.
indications: Adults with genotype 1 or 4 chronic HCV (no cirrhosis or compensated cirrhosis) in combination with peginterferon alfa and ribavirin
Adults with genotype 2 or 3 chronic HCV (no cirrhosis or compensated cirrhosis) in combination with ribavirin
Pediatric patients >=3 years with genotype 2 or 3 chronic HCV (no cirrhosis or compensated cirrhosis) in combination with ribavirin
As a component of a combination antiviral treatment regimen (not for monotherapy)

dosage.d: Sofosbuvir 400 mg once daily + peginterferon alfa + ribavirin
dosage.n: Ribavirin weight-based (<75 kg = 1000 mg, >=75 kg = 1200 mg) in two divided doses with food
May be considered when interferon-based regimen is not an option

dosage.t: Up to 48 weeks or until transplant, whichever is first

dosage.d: Weight-based sofosbuvir (tablets or oral pellets) + ribavirin
dosage.n: See label Table 3 for weight-based dosing

dosage.d: Weight-based sofosbuvir (tablets or oral pellets) + ribavirin
dosage.n: Follow Instructions for Use for oral pellets

admin: Test all patients for current or prior HBV infection (HBsAg and anti-HBc) before initiating therapy
Take one 400 mg tablet orally once daily with or without food
Always administer as part of a combination regimen with ribavirin, with or without peginterferon alfa
Do not miss or skip doses; take for the full prescribed duration based on genotype
Do not coadminister with amiodarone unless no alternative; if required, perform cardiac monitoring
moa: Sofosbuvir is a nucleotide prodrug inhibitor of the HCV NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, which is essential for viral replication. It undergoes intracellular metabolism to the pharmacologically active uridine analog triphosphate GS-461203, which is incorporated into HCV RNA by NS5B and acts as a chain terminator, halting viral replication. GS-461203 does not inhibit human DNA/RNA or mitochondrial RNA polymerases.

absolute: When used with ribavirin or peginterferon alfa/ribavirin, all contraindications to those agents apply (e.g., pregnancy in the patient or in a male's pregnant partner with ribavirin)
relative: Coadministration with amiodarone (not recommended; risk of serious bradycardia)
Coadministration with intestinal P-gp inducers such as rifampin or St. John's wort (not recommended)
Severe renal impairment (eGFR <30) or ESRD on hemodialysis (no dosing recommendation)
monitor: Concomitant amiodarone, especially with beta-blockers or advanced liver disease
Diabetic patients (risk of symptomatic hypoglycemia as hepatic function improves)

preg: When sofosbuvir is given with ribavirin or peginterferon alfa/ribavirin, the combination regimen is contraindicated in pregnant women and in men whose female partners are pregnant; refer to the ribavirin and peginterferon labeling for their pregnancy risks. No adequate human data exist for sofosbuvir alone; animal studies showed no adverse developmental effects at exposures above the human dose.
lact: It is not known whether sofosbuvir or its metabolites are present in human milk, affect milk production, or affect the breastfed infant. The metabolite GS-331007 was the primary component in milk of lactating rats without effect on pups. Weigh the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and any potential infant risk.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required for mild or moderate renal impairment. Safety and efficacy have not been established and no dosing recommendation can be given for severe renal impairment (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2) or ESRD requiring hemodialysis. Refer to ribavirin/peginterferon labeling for patients with CrCl <50 mL/min.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is required for mild, moderate, or severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A, B, or C). Safety and efficacy have not been established in patients with decompensated cirrhosis; note peginterferon alfa is contraindicated in hepatic decompensation.

major: Amiodarone - serious symptomatic bradycardia (incl. fatal cardiac arrest) with sofosbuvir-containing regimens; coadministration not recommended
Rifampin (intestinal P-gp inducer) - decreases sofosbuvir levels and efficacy; not recommended
St. John's wort (P-gp inducer) - decreases sofosbuvir levels and efficacy; not recommended
Other potent P-gp inducers (e.g., carbamazepine, phenytoin) - reduce sofosbuvir exposure; not recommended
moderate: Warfarin - HCV clearance may change hepatic function and alter INR; monitor closely
Antidiabetic agents - improved hepatic function may cause serious hypoglycemia; monitor glucose
Narrow-therapeutic-index CYP450 substrates such as certain immunosuppressants - monitor drug concentrations
minor: Beta-blockers - additive bradycardia risk in patients also taking amiodarone
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; a high-fat meal does not substantially affect exposure.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol, particularly in patients with advanced liver disease.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor INR in patients on warfarin and blood glucose in diabetic patients, as HCV clearance may alter hepatic function.

serious: Serious symptomatic bradycardia when coadministered with amiodarone
rare: Symptomatic hypoglycemia in diabetic patients (due to improved hepatic function)
emergency: HBV reactivation with fulminant hepatitis, hepatic failure and death
Serious symptomatic bradycardia or fatal cardiac arrest with amiodarone (near-syncope, syncope, chest pain, marked dizziness)

monitoring: Test all patients for HBV (HBsAg and anti-HBc) before initiating treatment
Monitor HCV/HBV coinfected patients for hepatitis flare or HBV reactivation during and after treatment
Cardiac monitoring (inpatient first 48 h, then daily for at least the first 2 weeks) if amiodarone coadministration is unavoidable
HCV RNA to assess virologic response; CBC for anemia when used with ribavirin/peginterferon
INR in patients on warfarin and blood glucose in diabetic patients
counsel: Take one 400 mg tablet once daily with the prescribed ribavirin-based regimen; do not miss or skip doses
Tell your provider about any history of hepatitis B infection
Seek immediate care for symptoms of bradycardia (fainting, dizziness, weakness, shortness of breath, chest pain) if taking amiodarone
Follow ribavirin pregnancy-prevention requirements for patients and male partners
Report all prescription, OTC and herbal products, including St. John's wort
pk: Rapid antiviral effect; chain termination of HCV RNA
Sofosbuvir Tmax ~0.5-2 h; metabolite GS-331007 ~2-4 h
Sofosbuvir ~0.4 h; metabolite GS-331007 ~27 h (median terminal)
Store below 30 C (86 F); dispense only in original container
pearls: BOXED WARNING: test all patients for HBV before treatment; HBV reactivation can be fatal, monitor coinfected patients during and after therapy
Always part of a combination regimen - never used as monotherapy; partner agent and duration are genotype-specific (G2 + RBV 12 wk, G3 + RBV 24 wk, G1/4 + PegIFN/RBV 12 wk)
Avoid amiodarone - serious symptomatic bradycardia and fatal cardiac arrest reported with sofosbuvir-containing regimens
No dosing recommendation for severe renal impairment or ESRD; renal clearance is the major route for the active metabolite GS-331007
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on the same day, then resume the regular once-daily schedule; do not double up. It is important not to miss or skip doses. Contact the prescriber if doses are missed.
overdose: The highest documented dose was a single 1200 mg dose (3x recommended) in 59 healthy subjects with no untoward effects. No specific antidote is available. Monitor for evidence of toxicity and provide general supportive care including vital signs and clinical observation. A 4-hour hemodialysis session removed about 18% of the administered dose.
